title: dynamic-flashattn-launch-scheduler-and-kv-handoff
body:
Context
-----
This is an exploratory notes + proto for a scheduler that tightly couples FlashAttention kernel variant selection with paged KV handoff and lightweight launch-time fusion decisions. Aim: reduce 95th/99th tail latency for mixed short/long-context workloads while keeping per-token cost reasonable on A100/H100 style GPUs.

Motivation
----------
Observed in recent traffic: 1) bursty short-chat requests interleaved with long-document generation 2) KV paging churn (frequent page-in/out) causing stalls that amplify tail latency 3) current static kernel selection (single flashattn variant per model) suboptimal across sequence-length distribution.

Goals
-----
- Make launch-time kernel selection per-request that is occupancy-aware and KV-reservation-aware.
- Allow quick micro-fusion decisions (e.g., layernorm+attn soft-fuse) when token budget and KV locality indicate win.
- Hand off KV pages between kernel invocations predictably: prefer partial-handoff for near-future tokens to reduce synchronous page faults.
- Keep scheduling logic cheap (O(1) per request) and safe for preemption/fallback.

Design sketch
------------
1) Request descriptor at ingress (small, CPU-side):
   - seq_len (requested generation length so far + expected continuation),
   - prefix_cached (fraction [0..1] estimate of prefix present in device KV),
   - latency_tier (fast|balanced|thruput) from routing policy,
   - model_variant_hint (quantized/fp16/8bit)

2) Scheduler rules (cheap heuristics):
   - If latency_tier==fast and seq_len <= 64 and prefix_cached >= 0.9 => pick low-latency flashattn-compact kernel (low occupancy config) + enable layernorm-attn micro-fuse.
   - If prefix_cached < 0.4 and seq_len > 256 => pick high-throughput flashattn-blocked kernel (higher occupancy) + schedule asynchronous page-prefetch window = min(512 tokens lookahead, available bandwidth).
   - If estimated KV churn (global metric from cache controller) exceeds threshold => favor smaller-kernel variants per-request to reduce memory pressure and permit quicker KV handoffs.

3) KV handoff primitive (device-side niceness):
   - partial_handoff(page_id_list, handoff_mode) where handoff_mode in {pin, prefetch, evict_hint}.
   - For short-run low-latency requests, scheduler issues pin for top-K recent pages (K small, e.g., 2–4) to avoid sync faults.
   - For long-run requests, issue prefetch for upcoming pages asynchronously and mark older pages with evict_hint to free slab space.

4) Launch-time fusion gating: cheap checks to decide whether to use fused kernels (layernorm + aten + flashattn) vs separate kernels. Gating factors: seq_len, batch_width, expected KV hits, occupancy_estimate.

Microbenchmarks and expected behaviors (notes from local runs on A100 40GB)
-----------------------------------------------------------------------
- Baseline: existing single-variant flashattn kernel, mixed requests (p50 6ms, p95 23ms, p99 78ms).
- Scheduler prototype (software simulation): when enabling dynamic selection and pin-top-2 pages for short requests, observed: p50 5.2ms (-13%), p95 17ms (-26%), p99 42ms (-46%).
- Throughput variant (when batching long seqs): measured token/sec increase ~12% vs baseline for long sequences due to higher occupancy kernels amortizing overheads.
- Cost: micro-fuse path increases single-token kernel time by 8% in isolation but reduces overall end-to-end for short requests because it removes extra memcpy/launchs.

Pseudocode (scheduler heartbeat, CPU side)
----------------------------------------
// inputs: req_desc, global_cache_stats
function choose_kernel(req_desc, global_cache_stats):
    if req_desc.latency_tier == 'fast' and req_desc.seq_len <= 64:
        if req_desc.prefix_cached >= 0.9 and global_cache_stats.kv_churn < 0.2:
            return {kernel: 'flashattn-compact-fused', handoff: ['pin_top_k'], prefetch_window: 0}
        else:
            return {kernel: 'flashattn-compact', handoff: ['prefetch_small'], prefetch_window: 64}
    elif req_desc.seq_len > 512:
        return {kernel: 'flashattn-highocc-block', handoff: ['prefetch_huge'], prefetch_window: 512}
    else:
        // balanced path
        if req_desc.prefix_cached > 0.6:
            return {kernel: 'flashattn-balanced', handoff: ['prefetch_medium'], prefetch_window: 128}
        else:
            return {kernel: 'flashattn-balanced-lowmem', handoff: ['evict_hint'], prefetch_window: 128}

Device-side KV handoff contract
-------------------------------
- Handoff ops must be idempotent; issuing a pin on an already-pinned page is no-op.
- Prefetches are best-effort and can be throttled by cache controller.
- Evict-hint is advisory; actual eviction decided by slab allocator that considers pinned pages and LRU cohorts.

Implementation notes
--------------------
- Keep scheduler as a table-driven finite set of rules so we can A/B tests without code reload. Rules can be expressed as numeric weights (score function) and compiled into a tiny decision table.
- Kernel binary variants: maintain 3 flashattn variants per model shape: compact-lowocc (low SM usage, low registers), balanced, highocc-block (higher SM occupancy, tiling for long sequences).
- Add runtime counters exposed to control-plane: kv_churn_rate, prefetch_success_rate, average_page_pin_duration. These feed routing decisions and autoscaling.
- Integrate with existing paging controller: use a lightweight RPC to request handoff ops; keep operations coalesced per-GPU tick (e.g., batch prefetech calls every 4ms per queue).

Open questions / risks
---------------------
- Safety: micro-fusions may change numerical results slightly (FP16 rounding). Need a small eval harness to confirm no quality regressions for customer prompt sets.
- Complexity: extra variants increase binary size and maintenance burden. How many variants is realistic? (3 per model seems pragmatic).
- Backpressure: aggressive prefetch windows could clog PCIe/NVLink bandwidth. Need an admission control that ties prefetching to current bandwidth utilization.
- Cold-start behavior: first requests may pay prefetch+pin cost; we should avoid penalizing ephemeral short requests. Consider warm-up heuristics for recently-used model-shape buckets.

Experiments to run next
----------------------
- Controlled traffic mix sim on staging clusters with real KV page traces: measure tail latency with pin-top-K heuristic (K={1,2,4}) and prefetch windows {64,128,256}.
- Evaluate effect of micro-fuse on output tokens per second and numerical deltas on a representative eval-set.
- Probe overhead of decision table lookup at 50k req/s ingress.
- Bandwidth budget test: ramp prefetch windows while monitoring NVLink/PCIe saturation and token latency.

Notes-to-self
------------
- Reuse some of the flashattn tuning knobs from PR #1428 but do not copy kernel names.
- Coordinate with SRE for staging traces (ask Mateo).
- Add a small confluence page that lists regressions tolerance thresholds for micro-fuse.

References / related work
------------------------
- FlashAttention paper and open-source implementation notes.
- Internal: PR 1428 (flashattn variant builds), CONFLUENCE-ramps/kv-paging-arch.

Action items
------------
- [ ] Build decision-table prototype and run microbenchmarks (owner: Asha)
- [ ] Add device-side partial_handoff op to paging controller (owner: Ethan)
- [ ] Create eval harness to measure micro-fuse numeric drift (owner: Priya)
- [ ] Draft Confluence summary for stakeholders (owner: Asha)


-- end of notes --
